title: Finding My Way Back
subtitle: How the Alaska Wilderness Restored My Perspective
bodyHtml:
For a long time, I lost touch with what I loved most: exploring the outdoors.
The long, dusty trails, the challenge of pushing past my limits, and the clarity
that comes with being surrounded by nature
— these were things I had set aside as I focused on my career.
But when I found myself feeling lost and unfulfilled,
I knew something had to change.

That’s how I ended up in Alaska, deep in the wilderness,
with an all-women crew of strangers.
I signed up for a 10-day expedition with the
National Outdoor Leadership School (NOLS),
an experience that was anything but easy.
NOLS isn’t for the weak.
It teaches not just how to survive in the wild, but how to thrive and lead.
At the start of our trip, we were flown in on a small plane
and dropped next to a melting glacier.
From there, we had to hike our way out over an entire mountain range
— no trails, no civilization, just our group, our gear, and the land.
